# Story 65 — Forgot password (reset via email) (Story: 65)

## Prerequisites

- Story 64 (Change password) — should land immediately before this story in the same feature. Story 64 is expected to introduce a **shared "post-password-change fallout" helper** (revoke every `RefreshFamily` for the user + send a "your password was changed" confirmation email). This story **reuses** that helper. If Story 64 has not yet extracted such a helper, this story's implementation must extract it (place under `backend/src/services/`, e.g. `passwordReset.service.ts` or `passwordChange.service.ts`) so both routes call it instead of duplicating logic.
- Coordinate with whoever owns `backend/src/services/email.service.ts` — this story adds two new transactional email templates that follow the existing `renderEmailHtml` shell.
- Rate-limiting of forgot-password requests is **out of scope** here (see intake "Out of scope"); flag as a follow-up for the `security-admin` feature.

---

## Story Goal

A customer, agent, or admin who has forgotten their password can reset it themselves without an admin intervening. The flow:

1. User visits a public **`/forgot-password`** page and submits their email address.
2. Backend always returns a generic 200 response (`"If an account exists for this email, we've sent a reset link"`) — no enumeration signal — and, when the email matches a real active user, generates a fresh single-use, 15-minute, **hashed** reset token, invalidates any earlier unused token for that user, and emails the reset link.
3. User clicks the link, lands on **`/reset-password?token=…`**, sets a new password (≥ 8 chars) + confirmation.
4. Backend hashes the incoming token with SHA-256, looks up the matching user, verifies the token is unexpired and unused, updates `User.passwordHash` (bcrypt), marks the token used, revokes **all** `RefreshFamily` sessions for the user, sends a "your password was changed" confirmation email, and writes an audit log entry.
5. Any invalid / expired / already-used token returns the same generic error without distinguishing the reason.

Not in scope: rate-limiting, admin-initiated reset, changing the account's email.

**File:** `backend/src/models/User.ts`

Add three fields to `IUser` (near the existing `emailConfirmToken` block at lines 52–53) and to the schema (near lines 115–116):

```ts
// IUser

```

- **Index on `passwordResetTokenHash`** because lookup is `User.findOne({ passwordResetTokenHash })`.

### 3 — Extract shared "post-password-change fallout" helper

**File (create if it does not already exist from Story 64):** `backend/src/services/passwordReset.service.ts`

Export:

```ts
import crypto from "crypto";
import { RefreshFamily } from "../models/RefreshFamily";
import { renderEmailHtml, sendEmail } from "./email.service";

export const RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000;

export function generateResetToken(): { rawToken: string; tokenHash: string } {
  const rawToken = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString("hex");
  const tokenHash = crypto.createHash("sha256").update(rawToken).digest("hex");
  return { rawToken, tokenHash };
}

export function hashResetToken(rawToken: string): string {
  return crypto.createHash("sha256").update(rawToken).digest("hex");
}

/**
 * Run after any password change (Story 64 change-password, Story 65 reset).
 * Revokes every active RefreshFamily for the user and emails a
 * "your password was changed" notice.
 *
 * `exemptFamilyId` lets Story 64 keep the caller's current session
 * alive; Story 65 always passes `undefined` because the caller was
 * logged out.
 */
export async function revokeAllSessionsAndNotify(params: {
  userId: string;
  userEmail: string;
  userName: string;
  exemptFamilyId?: string;
}): Promise<void> {
  const filter: Record<string, unknown> = { userId: params.userId, revoked: false };
  if (params.exemptFamilyId) filter.familyId = { $ne: params.exemptFamilyId };
  await RefreshFamily.updateMany(filter, { $set: { revoked: true } });

  // CLIENT_ORIGIN, not FRONTEND_BASE_URL — that env var doesn't exist in
  // this codebase. CLIENT_ORIGIN is the established name for "the
  // frontend's own origin, for building a link back to it" (already used
  // this way in me.routes.ts, ticket.routes.ts, slaMonitor.service.ts, and
  // already documented in backend/.env.example).
  const loginUrl = `${process.env.CLIENT_ORIGIN || "http://localhost:3000"}/login`;
  await sendEmail({
    to: params.userEmail,
    subject: "Your AzmSquad password was changed",
    text: `Hi ${params.userName},\n\nYour password was just changed. If this wasn't you, contact support immediately.\n\nSign in: ${loginUrl}`,
    html: renderEmailHtml({
      heading: "Your password was changed",
      bodyHtml: `<p>Hi ${params.userName},</p><p>Your AzmSquad password was just changed. If this wasn't you, contact support immediately.</p>`,
      ctaText: "Sign in",
      ctaUrl: loginUrl,
    }),
  });
}
```

- If Story 64 already introduced this helper under a different name/location, **use that one** instead — do not duplicate.
- Keep `generateResetToken` / `hashResetToken` in this same service so the two reset routes and their tests share one source of truth for the hashing choice.

### 4 — `POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password`

**File:** `backend/src/routes/auth.routes.ts` (append below existing routes, before `export default router`)

```ts
router.post(
  "/forgot-password",
  validateBody(forgotPasswordBodySchema),
  async (req: Request<unknown, unknown, ForgotPasswordBody>, res: Response) => {
    const genericResponse = {
      message: "If an account exists for this email, we've sent a reset link.",
    };

    const normalizedEmail = req.body.email.trim().toLowerCase();
    const user = await User.findOne({ email: normalizedEmail });

    // Silently no-op on unknown email or inactive account — same 200 shape,
    // same latency envelope (do NOT branch on user existence before res.json).
    if (!user || !user.isActive) {
      return res.json(genericResponse);
    }

    const { rawToken, tokenHash } = generateResetToken();
    user.passwordResetTokenHash = tokenHash;
    user.passwordResetTokenExpiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MS);
    user.passwordResetTokenUsedAt = null; // invalidate any prior unused token
    await user.save();

    const resetUrl = `${process.env.CLIENT_ORIGIN || "http://localhost:3000"}/reset-password?token=${rawToken}`;
    await sendEmail({
      to: user.email,
      subject: "Reset your AzmSquad password",
      text: `Hi ${user.name},\n\nClick the link below to reset your password. It expires in 15 minutes.\n\n${resetUrl}\n\nIf you didn't request this, you can ignore this email.`,
      html: renderEmailHtml({
        heading: "Reset your password",
        bodyHtml: `<p>Hi ${user.name},</p><p>Click the button below to reset your password. This link expires in 15 minutes. If you didn't request this, you can ignore this email.</p>`,
        ctaText: "Reset password",
        ctaUrl: resetUrl,
      }),
    });

    return res.json(genericResponse);
  }
);
```

- **Anti-enumeration:** the branch on `!user || !user.isActive` returns the identical response shape as the success branch. Do **not** add early `return` short-circuits that shortcut the async cost when the user does not exist — reviewers should not be able to distinguish the two paths by timing.
- Setting `passwordResetTokenUsedAt = null` on re-issue is what enforces AC "requesting a new reset link invalidates any earlier unused token" — the earlier `tokenHash` is overwritten too.
- No audit-log entry on request (the request itself is not privileged and could be abuse-noise).

### 5 — `POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password`

**File:** `backend/src/routes/auth.routes.ts` (immediately below `/forgot-password`)

```ts
router.post(
  "/reset-password",
  validateBody(resetPasswordBodySchema),
  async (req: Request<unknown, unknown, ResetPasswordBody>, res: Response) => {
    const genericError = { message: "This reset link is invalid or has expired." };

    const tokenHash = hashResetToken(req.body.token);
    const user = await User.findOne({ passwordResetTokenHash: tokenHash });

    if (
      !user ||
      !user.isActive ||
      !user.passwordResetTokenExpiresAt ||
      user.passwordResetTokenExpiresAt < new Date() ||
      user.passwordResetTokenUsedAt !== null
    ) {
      return res.status(400).json(genericError);
    }

    user.passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(req.body.newPassword, BCRYPT_SALT_ROUNDS);
    user.passwordResetTokenUsedAt = new Date();
    user.passwordResetTokenHash = null;         // one-shot: cannot be replayed
    user.passwordResetTokenExpiresAt = null;
    await user.save();

    await revokeAllSessionsAndNotify({
      userId: user.id,
      userEmail: user.email,
      userName: user.name,
      // no exemption — caller was logged out
    });

    await recordAuditLog({
      actor: String(user._id),
      action: "password_reset",
      targetType: "User",
      targetId: String(user._id),
      ipAddress: req.ip,
    });

    return res.json({ message: "Your password has been reset. You can now sign in." });
  }
);
```

- Single generic error covers "no such token", "token expired", and "token already used" — satisfies AC "without revealing which of those three was the reason".
- Nulling `passwordResetTokenHash` after use makes replay impossible even if the DB row is read directly.
- `action: "password_reset"` is the audit-log verb (do not add identifying detail for failed attempts — AC).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Unknown email submitted to `/forgot-password`** — 200 with the generic message, no email sent. Enforced at `auth.routes.ts` in the new route (Backend Task 4): the `if (!user || !user.isActive)` branch returns the same shape.
- **Inactive (deactivated) account requests reset** — treated the same as unknown email (silent no-op). Same enforcement point. Prevents deactivated accounts from being re-activated via the reset flow.
- **User requests a second reset link before consuming the first** — the second request overwrites `passwordResetTokenHash` / expiry and clears `passwordResetTokenUsedAt`, so the first link's SHA-256 no longer matches any stored hash → first link returns generic error. Enforced by the unconditional `user.save()` in Task 4.
- **Token expired (> 15 min)** — `passwordResetTokenExpiresAt < new Date()` branch in Task 5 returns generic error.
- **Token already consumed** — `passwordResetTokenUsedAt !== null` branch in Task 5. Because we also null out `passwordResetTokenHash` on consume, the lookup itself typically already misses; the `usedAt` check is defence-in-depth in case a future path leaves the hash intact.
- **Token from a user account that was deactivated after the link was issued** — `!user.isActive` branch in Task 5 returns generic error.
- **Two concurrent `/reset-password` submissions with the same token** — the first `await user.save()` nulls the hash; the second `findOne` misses and returns generic error. Race is safe (no double-apply).
- **Malformed body** (missing `email`, missing `token`, `newPassword` < 8 chars) — `validateBody` middleware returns a 400 with the zod error. Note this **is** a small enumeration signal ("valid email is required" vs generic success), but it's the same tradeoff already accepted for `/register` in this file.
- **SMTP unavailable / `SMTP_HOST` unset** — `sendEmail` logs a dry-run line and returns without throwing (see `email.service.ts:13–16, 67–70`); the reset row is still written. Local dev works without SMTP; the reset link is visible in the backend console log.
- **Unicode in email** — `.trim().toLowerCase()` matches the existing `/login` normalization at `auth.routes.ts:128`; do not add extra normalization (would drift from lookup key used elsewhere).
- **User clicks link, page loaded, then clicks again in a new tab** — the first submission consumes; the second gets generic error. Expected behaviour.
- **Reset link surfaced to an attacker via email forwarding** — 15-minute TTL + one-shot consume + `revokeAllSessionsAndNotify` sending the "your password was changed" email means the legitimate owner is notified as soon as the token is used.
- **Rate-limit abuse** — **NOT enforced by this story** (out of scope). Add a code comment above the new `/forgot-password` route: `// TODO(security-admin): rate-limit per IP + per email; tracked as a security-admin follow-up.`
- **Frontend `/reset-password` opened without `?token=`** — page renders the generic invalid-link message; no form submit is possible.

## Test Plan

Follow the existing patterns in `backend/tests/routes/*.routes.test.ts` (mongodb-memory-server + supertest) — see `backend/tests/routes/auth.routes.test.ts` if present, otherwise mirror `backend/tests/routes/me.routes.test.ts`.

1. **New file:** `backend/tests/routes/auth.forgotPassword.routes.test.ts` (or append a `describe("POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password", …)` block to the existing auth routes test file if one exists).
   1. Unknown email → 200 with generic message; no `passwordResetTokenHash` written anywhere.
   2. Inactive user → 200 with generic message; user's `passwordResetTokenHash` stays null.
   3. Active user → 200 with generic message; user document has `passwordResetTokenHash` set to a 64-char hex string, `passwordResetTokenExpiresAt` within ±5s of `now + 15min`, `passwordResetTokenUsedAt` null.
   4. Re-request → old hash is replaced (assert not equal), `expiresAt` advanced, `usedAt` null.
   5. Malformed body (no email) → 400 from `validateBody`.
2. **Same file (or sibling):** `describe("POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password", …)`.
   1. Valid token → 200 success message; `passwordHash` changed (bcrypt.compare with new password returns true, with old returns false); `passwordResetTokenHash` set to null; `passwordResetTokenUsedAt` set to a Date.
   2. Valid token → every prior `RefreshFamily` for this user has `revoked: true` (seed two families first, assert both revoked).
   3. Valid token → `AuditLog` collection has a new `password_reset` entry with `actor === user._id.toString()`.
   4. Valid token → "your password was changed" email attempt observable (SMTP dry-run console log — assert via a `vi.spyOn(console, "log")` or by asserting `sendEmail` was called with the expected subject if the test file already mocks `email.service`).
   5. Unknown token → 400 generic error, no user mutation.
   6. Expired token → 400 generic error (seed a user with expiry in the past).
   7. Already-used token → 400 generic error (seed with `usedAt !== null` and matching hash — even though the production path nulls the hash on consume, this exercises the defence-in-depth check).
   8. Token belonging to a now-inactive user → 400 generic error.
   9. Concurrent reset attempts (two `Promise.all` submissions with the same token) — exactly one 200 and one 400.
   10. Malformed body (no `token` or `newPassword` < 8 chars) → 400.
3. **New file (optional):** `backend/tests/services/passwordReset.service.test.ts` — unit tests for `generateResetToken` (returns different tokens each call; `hashResetToken(rawToken) === tokenHash`), `hashResetToken` (deterministic), and `revokeAllSessionsAndNotify` (bulk-revokes; respects `exemptFamilyId`).
4. **Frontend smoke** (manual is acceptable if no Playwright suite exists for auth):

   - Visit `/forgot-password` → submit real email → check backend console for the reset link → open in a new tab → set new password → success screen → redirected to `/login` → sign in with new password succeeds.
   - Visit `/reset-password` (no token) → generic invalid-link message.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Schema addition only** — three new nullable fields on `User`. No data migration required; existing users read back `null` for the new fields on first access.
- **Rollback:** the code changes can be reverted without a schema rollback; the three new fields simply go unused. If you want to purge them post-rollback: `db.users.updateMany({}, { $unset: { passwordResetTokenHash: "", passwordResetTokenExpiresAt: "", passwordResetTokenUsedAt: "" } })`.
- **Half-applied state:** if backend is deployed before frontend, the two routes exist but nothing calls them — safe. If frontend is deployed before backend, the two pages render but form submissions return 404 — visible failure, not silent corruption; deploy backend first.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** run `npm run build` in `backend/` — no TypeScript errors.
2. **Backend tests:** run `npm test` in `backend/` — new suites green, no regression in existing `auth.routes.test.ts` / `me.routes.test.ts`.
3. **Backend lint:** `npm run lint` in `backend/` if the project has a lint script.
4. **Frontend builds:** run `npm run build` in `frontend/` — confirms the new Server Actions' `"use server"` boundary + shared-lib imports typecheck under production build (per memory: "'use server' needed when Client Component imports a shared lib directly").
5. **Frontend runs:** run `npm run dev` in `frontend/` and `npm run dev` in `backend/`. Walk the four manual flows in Test Plan §4.
6. **Regression:** log in with an existing seeded account, then reset that account's password via the flow, then log in with the new password — succeeds. Old sessions (open the app in a second browser first, then reset from the first browser) — the second browser should be logged out on its next authenticated request.
7. **i18n:** switch locale toggle to Arabic on `/forgot-password`, `/reset-password`, and the login page — no missing keys, no untranslated English fragments.
8. **SEO:** view page source of `/forgot-password` and `/reset-password` in dev — `<title>` and `<meta name="description">` are the page-specific strings, not the app default.

## Done Criteria

- [x] Public `POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password` returns the same generic 200 response for every email (known / unknown / inactive).
- [x] Reset tokens are stored on `User` as SHA-256 hashes; raw tokens never touch the database.
- [x] Reset tokens expire 15 minutes after issue.
- [x] Requesting a new reset link invalidates any earlier unused token for the same account (verified by test).
- [x] Reset email is sent via `email.service.ts` using the `renderEmailHtml` shell.
- [x] Public `POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password` accepts `{ token, newPassword }`, validates `newPassword` ≥ 8 chars, updates `passwordHash` via bcrypt, marks the token used, and cannot be replayed.
- [x] Invalid / expired / already-used tokens all return the same generic error.
- [x] On successful reset, every active `RefreshFamily` for the user is revoked.
- [x] On successful reset, the user receives a "your password was changed" confirmation email.
- [x] On successful reset, an `AuditLog` entry with action `password_reset` is written; failed attempts are not audit-logged with identifying detail.
- [x] Frontend page `/forgot-password` exists, is public, has page-specific SEO metadata, and is reachable from a "Forgot password?" link on the login form.
- [x] Frontend page `/reset-password` exists, is public, has page-specific SEO metadata, consumes `?token=` from the URL, and posts to the reset endpoint.
- [x] i18n keys for both new pages and the new login link exist in both `en.json` and `ar.json`.
- [x] Shared post-password-change helper (`revokeAllSessionsAndNotify` or Story 64's equivalent) is called from a single place — no duplicated revoke+notify code between Story 64 and Story 65.
- [x] `// TODO(security-admin): rate-limit …` comment left above `/forgot-password`.
